predecessors.name: Kingdom of Macedon
predecessors.text: Babylon: 'It was held at Babylon in June 323 BC'; Perdiccas became 'Regent of the Empire' there

successors.name: Kingdom of Macedon
successors.text: Babylonia, held by the empire after the regent's death: Seleucus 'only became satrap of Babylonia at the second partition (the Partition of Triparadisus)'

successors.name: Seleucid Empire
successors.text: Cliopatria's first Seleucid shape (318-316) has the same bounding box as Perdiccas's

ledger.x: 323: At the Partition of Babylon, 'held at Babylon in June 323 BC', Perdiccas becomes Regent of the Empire (epimeletes) and holds the council 'as Hegemon' that assigns the satrapies.
323: the regency's Babylonia counts as the empire's own tint.
320: the regency ends with Perdiccas's death.
320: Perdiccas is murdered by his officers.

wars.name: Perdiccas' campaign in Cappadocia
wars.outcome: 'in the early summer of 322 BC Perdiccas marched with the imperial army'; he defeated the satrap Ariarathes I in two battles, then took him captive, tortured and killed him.

wars.name: Perdiccas' invasion of Egypt
wars.outcome: Failed at the Nile crossings; the army mutinied and killed Perdiccas in 320.

certainty.note: The seat of an imperial regency has no borders drawn by any page.
